div.head: Ps Cn for 9
div.ab: Sintque omnes, tam primarii quam mediocres et minuti, immunes, liberi et quieti ab omnibus prouincialibus summonitionibus et popularibus placitis, que hundredlaghe Angli dicunt, et ab omnibus armorum oneribus, quod warscot Angli dicunt, et forinsecis querelis.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 621 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: And let all, chief men as well as middling and lesser, be exempt, free and quit of all provincial summonses and popular pleas, which the English call hundredlaghe (hundred-law), and of all burdens of arms, which the English call warscot (war-tax), and of outside suits.

note.seg: diese Exemtion von Gerichtsfolge zu Grafschaft und Hundred setzten die Forstbeamten nicht durch: noch 1222 ist nur consuetudo: uiridarii poni non debent in assisis, recognicionibus uel iuratis; ebensowenig die Erbförster; Turner p. xx; xxiv

The forest officials did not achieve this exemption from suit of court to shire and hundred: even in 1222 it is only consuetudo: uiridarii poni non debent in assisis, recognicionibus uel iuratis; nor did the hereditary foresters; Turner p. xx; xxiv.

Hale (Domesday of S. Paul's p. lxxxiij) identificirt das Wort mit lagehundred: Gerichtstag der Hundertschaft; gemeint ist jedenfalls, was Urkunden 12. Jhs. hundred nennen: Gerichtsfolgepflicht (lagu: ‘Pflicht’ auch Rect. 1), vielleicht auch im besonderen (wie Ducange zu eng erklärt) die Geldstrafe für deren Versäumniss, genau wie lex episcopalis Wl ep. 3, 2 f

Hale (Domesday of S. Paul's p. lxxxiii) identifies the word with lagehundred: court day of the hundred; at any rate what is meant is what 12th-century charters call hundred: the obligation of suit of court (lagu: 'obligation' also Rect. 1), perhaps also in particular (as Ducange explains, too narrowly) the money penalty for failing in it, exactly like lex episcopalis Wl ep. 3, 2 f.

w[e]ar[d]peni[ng] (Wachtabgabe) ersetzt die Last des Wachehaltens (Inquis. Cantabrig. 59 = Domesday I 190a 1) und gebührt dem Staate im Grafschaftsgericht (Hale Dom. Paul's p. lxxviij ff. ciii ff.); Eadward III. befreite Hulm von wardpeni (Kemble Cod. dipl. *785), Wilhelm I. Battle von warpeni: Chron. de Bello p. 24. [Auch Romscot und Rompening bedeuten Eine Abgabe.] Vgl. die Freiheit der Exchequerbeamten von gewissen Steuern; Dial. de Scacc. I 8D, ed. Hughes p. 95. — Ein balliuus forestae tenuit X feoda militum, de quorum seruicio exoneratus fuit propter custodiam foreste; a. 1289; bei Turner 67

w[e]ar[d]peni[ng] (watch-due) replaces the burden of keeping watch (Inquis. Cantabrig. 59 = Domesday I 190a 1) and is owed to the state in the shire court (Hale, Dom. Paul's p. lxxviii ff., ciii ff.); Edward [the Confessor, 'Eadward III.'] freed Hulme from wardpeni (Kemble, Cod. dipl. *785), William I freed Battle from warpeni: Chron. de Bello p. 24. [Romscot and Rompening likewise denote one and the same due.] Cf. the exemption of Exchequer officials from certain taxes; Dial. de Scacc. I 8 D, ed. Hughes p. 95. — A balliuus forestae tenuit X feoda militum, de quorum seruicio exoneratus fuit propter custodiam foreste; 1289; in Turner 67.

forinsecus heisst nicht bloss ‘ausserforstlich’, sondern, wie sonst bei königl. Exemtionen Privilegierter, ‘Staatsanspruch an Grundbesitz allgemein’; vgl. Gl utware; o. S. 258, Z. 23 v. u.

forinsecus means not merely ‘outside the forest’ but, as elsewhere in royal exemptions of privileged persons, ‘the State’s claim on landed property in general’; cf. Gl utware; above p. 258, line 23 from the bottom
